transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squeal for the first few minutes that then fades, while it still dries, is most often a dry/worn jockey (belt-tension) pulley or a glazed belt when cold. Something caught around the drum or filter is also possible; a drum roller/bearing is less likely unless there is a rumble or rough feel as well. Switch it off, unplug it and let it cool. Check the empty drum, its lifters, lint filter and filter slot for coins, hair grips or anything rubbing, then slowly turn the drum by hand and listen. Does it turn smoothly and quietly, or does it squeak, feel rough or rumble? If the squeal is worsening or the drum becomes hard to turn, stop using it and arrange a dryer engineer before the belt or pulley fails.
Unplugged it and turned the drum by hand. It turns, but there's a slight squeak/scrape and feels a little rough. Nothing stuck in the door seal or filter that I can see.

That makes an internal drum-drive fault much more likely than something trapped. The startup squeal that fades is most typical of a dry/worn jockey (belt-tension) pulley or a glazed belt; the slight rough scrape by hand also leaves a drum support roller or bearing in the running. With it still unplugged and empty, gently lift the front edge of the drum upwards and let it down again. Obvious up-and-down movement or a clunk points more towards drum rollers/bearing; if it stays firm, the jockey pulley/belt is the stronger suspect. Either repair requires opening the dryer, so avoid prolonged use if the noise worsens, the drum starts catching, or there is a hot-rubber smell, and arrange a dryer engineer rather than trying to run it until it fails.
I'm not sure how to check that, sorry. I've got a bad back so I can't tilt or lay the dryer down, and I'm not sure how to lift the drum at the front from the outside. Is there another way to tell?

Yes — but there is not a reliable external check that will separate the jockey pulley/belt from a drum roller or bearing, and you do not need to lift, tilt or dismantle it. The cold-start squeal that fades, together with the rough/scraping feel when turned by hand, makes an internal drum-drive part the likely cause: most likely the jockey (idler) pulley or belt, with a drum support roller/bearing also possible. These need the dryer opened to confirm, so I’d arrange a tumble-dryer engineer rather than risk aggravating it. Stop using it sooner if the squeal becomes constant, the drum starts catching, there is a hot-rubber/burning smell, or it stops turning.

candidates: Jockey/idler pulley or belt becoming noisy when cold (high)
Loose item or debris rubbing in the drum/filter area (medium)
Drum support roller or bearing wear (low)
